Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a historical running-rehabilitation note for March 21-25, 2025. Record the first continuous run result, the limit for the rest of March, and the next planned short run.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Historical running-rehabilitation note — March 21–25, 2025", "body": "## Running rehabilitation note
**Date range:** March 21–25, 2025

- **First continuous run:** Friday, March 21 — 15 minutes of easy continuous running on the morning lake-trail route. On Saturday, March 22, ordinary walking and stairs remained free of the focal inside-right-ankle ache. This was a symptom check through the next morning, not a return to the former three-mile routine.
- **Limit for the rest of March:** Keep to two short, nonconsecutive running sessions per week. Do not increase both duration and frequency in the same week. Continue ankle-and-calf strengthening and check symptoms during each run and through the following day.
- **Next planned short run:** Tuesday morning, March 25 — a 15-minute continuous easy run, keeping the reduced load. Stop for focal ankle pain or a gait change; check symptoms later that day and the following day.", "folder": "Health"}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_028_01", "path": "args", "criterion": "The note says Riley completed a first 15-minute continuous easy run on March 21, 2025 and remained free of the focal inside-right-ankle ache during next-morning walking and stairs; she would keep two nonconsecutive short runs per week for the rest of March rather than return to three-mile runs or add a third weekly run; and her next short run was planned for the morning of March 25.", "value": {"title": "Historical running-rehabilitation note — March 21–25, 2025", "body": "## Running rehabilitation note
**Date range:** March 21–25, 2025

- **First continuous run:** Friday, March 21 — 15 minutes of easy continuous running on the morning lake-trail route. On Saturday, March 22, ordinary walking and stairs remained free of the focal inside-right-ankle ache. This was a symptom check through the next morning, not a return to the former three-mile routine.
- **Limit for the rest of March:** Keep to two short, nonconsecutive running sessions per week. Do not increase both duration and frequency in the same week. Continue ankle-and-calf strengthening and check symptoms during each run and through the following day.
- **Next planned short run:** Tuesday morning, March 25 — a 15-minute continuous easy run, keeping the reduced load. Stop for focal ankle pain or a gait change; check symptoms later that day and the following day.", "folder": "Health"}}]}

{"results":[{"check_id":"riley_028_01","passed":true,"reason":"The note records a first “15 minutes of easy continuous running” on Friday, March 21, with next-morning “walking and stairs” free of the focal inside-right-ankle ache; limits the rest of March to “two short, nonconsecutive running sessions per week” and says this is “not a return to the former three-mile routine”; and plans the next short run for “Tuesday morning, March 25.”"}]}
